name: Colossus
reason: gate passed; run with --promote to apply
evidence_url: The xAI Colossus supercomputer is located at 3231 Paul R. Lowry Road in South Memphis, Tennessee, in a 785,000 square foot former Electrolux manufacturing facility situated on over 217 acres. An affiliate of Phoenix Investors acquired the building in December 2023. By March 2024 the property was leased to xAI. They took over the factory with the goal of building the world's largest supercomputer, named Colossus, to fuel artificial intelligence, with more than a dozen generators steadily burning methane gas visible at the site as early as September 2024. In November 2024, TVA approved xAI's request for over 100 MW of grid power supplied through MLGW, upgrading from an initial grid connection of only 8 MW (local news asserts Musk has said the site needs 150 MW). xAI submitted a contract to purchase 13 acres of City of Memphis-owned land at 2685 Plant Road, located on the south side of the T.E. Maxson Wastewater Treatment Facility, through its affiliate CTC Property LLC, for $820,000. The proposed Colossus Water Recycling Plant will process municipal wastewater from the T.E. Maxson Wastewater Treatment Plant with a planned capacity of 10.4 million gallons per day. TVA and Nucor Steel have signed Letters of Intent to purchase water from the facility alongside xAI, with peak demand by all three facilities estimated at 12.5 million gallons per day.

name: Colossus 2
reason: gate passed; run with --promote to apply
evidence_url: This project shares its history with Colossus, and is an expansion of the initial site, located at 5420 Tulane Road. Based on satellite imagery and analysis of the cooling equipment, SemiAnalysis estimated Colossus 2 is progressing toward 400 MW of critical IT capacity, with a hybrid cooling system of approximately 130 dry coolers and 135 adiabatic cooling units, producing an estimated annual water footprint of approximately 346 million gallons per year (roughly 0.9 million gallons per day).
